summary.en: Swallowed by a great fish, he called out to Allah from three darknesses, and was answered.
summary.ur: مچھلی کے پیٹ میں، تین اندھیروں سے انہوں نے اللہ کو پکارا، اور اللہ نے ان کی پکار سن لی۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
Imagine being in a place so dark that you cannot see your own hand.
No light, no sound, and no one who knows where you are.
And yet, from that place, one man called out to Allah... and Allah heard him.
This is the story of Prophet Yunus, peace be upon him.
In the Quran he is also called Dhun-Nun, the man of the fish.
Allah says about him:
And indeed, Yunus was one of the messengers.
Allah sent Yunus to a great city.
The scholars of tafsir say it was Nineveh, in the land of Iraq.
The Quran tells us that its people were a hundred thousand or more.
They did not worship Allah alone.
So Yunus called them to Him.
He reminded them, he warned them, and he gave them time.
But they turned away, and they would not listen.
In the end, Yunus left them in anger.
The scholars explain that he left before Allah had given him permission to go.
He walked away from his people, and went down to the sea.
He ran to a ship that was fully loaded.
The ship was heavy, and the scholars of tafsir mention that the waves rose high around it, and everyone on board was in danger.
They decided that someone had to leave the ship to make it lighter, and they drew lots to choose.
The lot fell on Yunus.
He was thrown into the sea, and a huge fish swallowed him, while he was blaming himself for what he had done.
But the fish did not harm him.
Some of the early scholars mention that Allah commanded it not to break a single bone, and not to hurt his flesh.
Allah kept him alive, inside the belly of the fish.
Now Yunus was in darkness upon darkness.
Companions of the Prophet, like Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn Abbas,
explained that it was the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness inside the fish.
There was no one to call for help.
No ship, no family, no people.
Only Allah.
So Yunus did not complain, and he did not blame anyone else.
He turned to his Lord, he glorified Him, and he admitted his own mistake.
Listen to his words, as Allah tells them in the Quran:
There is no god but You.
Glory be to You.
Truly, I was one of the wrongdoers.
In just a few words, Yunus said everything.
He declared that Allah alone is God.
He declared that Allah is perfect, and free of every fault.
And he admitted that the mistake was his own.
And Allah answered him:
So We answered him, and saved him from his distress.
And that is how We save the believers.
Notice the last part.
Allah did not only save Yunus.
He tells us that He saves the believers in the same way.
This dua is not only for Yunus.
It is for all of us.
Allah also tells us why Yunus was saved.
He was a man who glorified Allah often, long before he was ever in trouble:
Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah,
he would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the Day that people are raised again.
The remembrance he made in good times was there for him in his hardest moment.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him,
taught the same lesson: know Allah in times of ease, and He will know you in times of hardship.
Then Allah commanded the fish, and it cast Yunus out onto the shore.
He was thrown onto an open shore, weak and ill.
Abdullah ibn Mas'ud described him as being like a newly hatched chick, with no feathers at all.
There was no shade and no shelter.
So Allah made a gourd plant grow over him.
Its wide leaves shaded him and protected him, while he slowly regained his strength.
And what happened to his people, back in the city?
The scholars of tafsir mention that after Yunus left, they began to see signs of the punishment he had warned them about.
They were afraid.
They went out together, with their families and their children, and they cried to Allah, and repented sincerely.
And Allah accepted their repentance.
The Quran tells us that this did not happen to any other town:
Of all the towns that were warned, only the people of Yunus believed in time, and their belief saved them.
Allah lifted the punishment from them, and let them enjoy their lives for a while.
The scholars mention that when Yunus was strong again, he went back to his people, and found that they had believed.
Allah says:
And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
And they believed, so We let them enjoy life for a while.
So what can we take from the story of Yunus, peace be upon him?
First: no darkness is too deep for Allah.
Not a storm, not the sea, not the belly of a fish.
Whatever you are going through, He hears you.
Second: when we make a mistake, the way back is to admit it honestly, and turn to Allah, just as Yunus did.
Third: the remembrance we make in easy times helps us in hard times.
So make it a habit now.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said that the dua of Dhun-Nun,
which he made in the belly of the fish, is never made by a Muslim for anything, except that Allah answers him.
This was reported by Imam at-Tirmidhi.
And the Prophet also said: no servant of Allah should say, I am better than Yunus, the son of Matta.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
Every prophet of Allah deserves our love and our respect.
Let us end by listening to the dua of Yunus, once more.
May Allah make us among those who remember Him in times of ease, and who turn to Him in every hardship.
And may He answer our duas, as He answered the dua of Yunus.
This was the story of Prophet Yunus, peace be upon him.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

summary.en: Hunted by Quraysh and hidden in a cave, the Prophet, peace be upon him, set out for Madinah, and a new chapter of Islam began.
summary.ur: قریش کے تعاقب میں، غار میں چھپ کر، نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم مدینہ روانہ ہوئے، اور اسلام کا ایک نیا باب شروع ہوا۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
In this episode, a story from the life of our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
It was a journey of more than four hundred kilometres, across the desert, from Makkah to Madinah.
And it changed the history of the world.
In the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, the Muslims chose this journey as the start of the Islamic calendar,
and we still count our years from it today.
This is the story of the Hijrah.
For thirteen years, the Prophet called the people of Makkah to worship Allah alone.
Some believed.
But most of the leaders of Quraysh rejected him, and they made life hard for everyone who followed him.
Believers were mocked, beaten, and boycotted.
Then, in the season of Hajj, a few men from Yathrib,
the city that would come to be called Madinah, met the Prophet and accepted Islam.
The next year, more of them came.
And the year after that,
more than seventy of them gave him their pledge: that they would protect him as they protected their own families.
The doors of Madinah were opening.
So the Prophet allowed the Muslims to emigrate.
Quietly, in small groups, they began to leave Makkah, leaving behind their homes and their wealth, for the sake of Allah.
Quraysh were alarmed.
If the Prophet reached Madinah, Islam would have a home, and a people ready to defend it.
The books of Seerah record that their leaders met together and agreed on a plan.
Young men from many different clans would strike him at the same moment,
so that his blood would be on every clan, and no single family could be blamed.
Allah tells us about that plot in the Quran:
And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to hold you captive, or kill you, or drive you out.
They were planning, and Allah was planning.
And Allah is the best of planners.
Allah gave His Messenger permission to leave.
Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, describes what happened next.
The Prophet came to the house of her father, Abu Bakr,
in the heat of midday, at a time he never usually came, with his head covered.
He said:
I have been given permission to leave.
Abu Bakr asked:
Will I be your companion, O Messenger of Allah?
And he said:
Yes.
Abu Bakr had been feeding two camels for months, ready for this very day.
He offered one to the Prophet, and the Prophet accepted it only on the condition that he paid for it.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
They prepared food for the journey in a hurry.
Asma, the daughter of Abu Bakr, had nothing to tie the bag of food with,
so she tore her waistband in two, and tied it with one half.
From that day she was known as Dhat an-Nitaqayn, the woman of the two waistbands.
The books of Seerah record that the Prophet left his house that night while the young men of Quraysh were waiting outside,
and that Ali ibn Abi Talib lay in his bed, so they would think he was still there.
As he left, the Prophet looked back at Makkah and said:
By Allah, you are the best land of Allah, and the most beloved land of Allah to Allah.
And had I not been driven out of you, I would never have left.
This was reported by Imam at-Tirmidhi.
Abdullah ibn Abbas explained that when the Prophet was commanded to emigrate, Allah revealed this ayah:
And say:
My Lord, let me enter with a good entrance, and let me leave with a good exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.
Instead of taking the road north towards Madinah, they went south, to a mountain called Thawr, and hid in a cave near its top.
They stayed there for three nights.
Each night, Abu Bakr's son Abdullah came to them in secret with the news of Makkah,
and left before dawn so that no one would notice he had been away.
And Amir ibn Fuhayrah, who looked after Abu Bakr's sheep, grazed them near the cave, and brought them milk to drink.
Meanwhile, Quraysh were searching everywhere.
They promised a reward to anyone who brought them back: a hundred camels for each of them.
Then the searchers came right up to the cave.
Abu Bakr could see their feet.
He whispered:
O Messenger of Allah, if one of them just looked down below his feet, he would see us.
And the Prophet answered him with words of complete trust:
What do you think, Abu Bakr, of two, when Allah is the third of them?
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Allah mentions this very moment in the Quran:
If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him, when the disbelievers drove him out,
the second of two, when the two were in the cave, and he said to his companion:
Do not grieve, Allah is with us.
And Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him.
After three nights, a guide they had hired met them at the cave with the camels.
He was not a Muslim, but he knew the desert well, and they trusted him.
He led them along a route near the coast that few people used.
They travelled through the night, and rested in the heat of the day.
Then a horseman came after them.
His name was Suraqa ibn Malik, and he wanted the reward.
Suraqa himself described what happened.
He came close enough to hear the Prophet reciting the Quran.
Abu Bakr kept looking back, but the Prophet did not turn around once.
Then the legs of Suraqa's horse sank into the ground, up to the knees, and he fell.
He got up and tried again, and again the horse sank.
Suraqa understood that this man was protected.
He called out to them, asking for safety, and offered them food and supplies.
They took nothing from him, and only asked him to keep their journey a secret.
He asked for a written promise of safety, and the Prophet had it written for him.
Suraqa rode back, and every searcher he met on the way, he turned around, saying: there is no one out here.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
In Madinah, the Muslims had heard that the Prophet had left Makkah.
Every morning they went out to the edge of the city to wait for him, until the midday heat drove them back home.
One day, just after they had gone back,
a man standing high on a fort saw travellers in white appearing out of the shimmering heat, and he shouted at the top of his voice:
Here is the one you have been waiting for!
The Muslims rushed out to meet him.
The Prophet first stopped at Quba, at the edge of Madinah, and stayed there for more than ten nights.
There he founded the Masjid of Quba, the first mosque he built.
Then he rode into the city.
His camel walked on until it knelt in an open yard that belonged to two orphan boys.
The Prophet bought the land from them, and there the Muslims built his mosque, al-Masjid an-Nabawi.
The people of Madinah, the Ansar, welcomed the emigrants, the Muhajirun,
into their homes, and shared everything they had with them.
Allah praised them in the Quran:
And those who settled in the city and in faith before them, love those who emigrated to them,
and find no envy in their hearts for what the emigrants were given.
They put others before themselves, even when they are in need.
And whoever is saved from the greed of his own soul, it is they who will succeed.
So what can we take from the Hijrah?
First: trust Allah, and do everything you can.
The Prophet prepared the camels, hired a guide, chose a hidden route, and hid in a cave.
And still his heart rested on Allah alone:
Do not grieve, Allah is with us.
Second: nothing given up for Allah is ever lost.
The emigrants left their homes and their wealth, and Allah gave them a new home,
a new family in faith, and honour in this world and the next.
Third: everything depends on the intention.
The Prophet said:
Actions are only by intentions, and everyone will have what they intended.
So whoever emigrated for Allah and His Messenger, their emigration is for Allah and His Messenger.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
May Allah give us hearts like the hearts of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and make every step we take be for Him.
This was the story of the Hijrah.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

tagline.en: From the well to the palace

summary.en: Thrown into a well by his brothers and jailed though innocent, he stayed patient, and Allah raised him to rule Egypt.
summary.ur: بھائیوں نے کنویں میں ڈالا، بےقصور قید ہوئے، مگر صبر کیا، اور اللہ نے انہیں مصر کا حاکم بنا دیا۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
Allah calls it the best of stories.
A whole surah of the Quran tells it from beginning to end: a story of jealousy and patience,
of a well, a prison and a palace, and of a father who never gave up hope.
This is the story of Prophet Yusuf, peace be upon him.
It begins with a dream.
One night the young Yusuf saw a dream, and he told his father about it:
O my father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon.
I saw them bowing down to me.
His father was Prophet Yaqub, peace be upon him.
He understood that the dream was a sign of something great for his son,
and he told him: do not tell your brothers about your dream, or they will plot against you.
Yusuf had eleven brothers, and ten of them were older.
They were jealous of how much their father loved Yusuf and his younger brother, Binyamin.
They said to each other: kill Yusuf, or throw him away to some distant land, and our father will be ours alone.
One of them said: do not kill him.
Throw him into the bottom of a well, and some travellers will pick him up.
So they asked their father to let Yusuf go out with them, and promised to take care of him.
When they were far from home, they threw him down into the well.
But Allah inspired Yusuf: one day you will tell them about what they have done, while they do not know who you are.
That night they came back to their father, weeping.
They said a wolf had eaten Yusuf while they were racing, and they showed him his shirt, stained with false blood.
Yaqub knew they were not telling the truth.
And he said:
Rather, your souls have made something seem right to you.
So patience is most fitting.
And it is Allah whose help is sought against what you describe.
Some travellers stopped by the well and let down a bucket for water, and up came a boy.
They took him to Egypt and sold him for a few coins.
The man who bought him was a great minister of Egypt, the Aziz.
He told his wife: make his stay comfortable; perhaps he will be of benefit to us, or we will adopt him as a son.
Yusuf grew up in that house, and Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge.
Then came a hard test.
The wife of the Aziz wanted him for herself.
She closed the doors and called him to her.
But Yusuf said:
I seek refuge in Allah.
He refused her, and ran for the door.
She caught his shirt from behind and tore it, and at the door they found her husband.
She blamed Yusuf.
But a witness from her own family said: look at the shirt.
It was torn from the back, so he was the one running away.
The truth was clear.
Still, the talk spread through the city, and the women of the city pressed Yusuf too.
So Yusuf turned to his Lord and said:
My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they call me to.
And unless You turn their plot away from me, I might incline towards them, and be among the ignorant.
So Allah turned their plot away from him.
And even though he had done nothing wrong, Yusuf was put in prison.
Even in prison, he called people to Allah.
Two young men there each saw a dream,
and Yusuf explained them: one would go free and serve the king again, and the other would be put to death.
It happened just as he said.
Yusuf asked the one who went free to mention him to the king.
But the man forgot, and Yusuf stayed in prison for several more years.
Then the king of Egypt saw a dream that no one could explain: seven fat cows being eaten by seven thin ones,
and seven green ears of grain, and seven dry.
At last, the man from the prison remembered Yusuf.
Yusuf explained it: seven years of good harvests would come, then seven years of hard famine.
Store the grain while you can.
The king sent for him.
But Yusuf would not leave the prison until his name was cleared.
The women were asked, and even the wife of the Aziz said: now the truth has come out.
It was I who tried to tempt him, and he is truthful.
The king brought Yusuf close and trusted him.
Yusuf asked to be put in charge of the storehouses of the land, and Allah established him in Egypt.
The famine came, and it reached the land where Yaqub and his sons lived.
The brothers travelled to Egypt to buy grain, and they stood before Yusuf.
He knew them at once, but they did not recognise him.
Yusuf asked them to bring their youngest brother, Binyamin, next time.
When they came back with him, Yusuf quietly told Binyamin who he was.
Then, by a plan that Allah made for him, he kept Binyamin with him in Egypt.
Back home, their father's grief returned, deeper than ever.
He wept for Yusuf until his eyes turned white.
His sons said: you will wear yourself out remembering Yusuf.
And Yaqub answered:
I only complain of my sorrow and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
Then he told them: go and search for Yusuf and his brother, and never lose hope in the mercy of Allah.
So they went back to Egypt, humble and in need, and asked Yusuf for charity.
And Yusuf said to them: do you know what you did to Yusuf and his brother?
They looked at him and said: are you really Yusuf?
He said:
I am Yusuf, and this is my brother.
Allah has been gracious to us.
Whoever is mindful of Allah and patient, Allah never lets the reward of those who do good be lost.
They said: by Allah, Allah has preferred you over us, and we were truly wrong.
And Yusuf answered them:
No blame upon you today.
May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.
Yusuf gave them his shirt and said: lay it over my father's face, and his sight will return.
As the caravan left Egypt, far away, Yaqub said:
I can sense the scent of Yusuf.
And when the shirt was laid over his face, he could see again.
The whole family came to Egypt.
Yusuf raised his parents up onto the throne, and they all bowed down before him,
as a greeting of honour that was allowed in their time, though not in ours.
And Yusuf said:
O my father, this is the meaning of my dream from long ago.
My Lord has made it come true.
Then Yusuf turned to his Lord in a beautiful prayer:
My Lord, You have given me some of the kingdom, and taught me the meaning of dreams.
Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the next.
Let me die as a Muslim, and join me with the righteous.
So what can we take from the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him?
First:
Allah's plan is often hidden.
The well led to the palace, and the prison led to the throne.
What looks like loss may be the road to something better.
Second: patience is beautiful.
Yaqub waited for years, and complained only to Allah, and he never lost hope in His mercy.
Third: forgiveness is strength.
When Yusuf finally had power over his brothers, he chose to forgive them.
And fourth: purity is worth any price.
Yusuf chose prison over sin, and Allah raised him for it.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, described Yusuf as the most honourable of people: a prophet,
the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of Allah's close friend, Ibrahim.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
May Allah give us the patience of Yaqub, the purity of Yusuf, and hearts that forgive.
This was the story of Prophet Yusuf, peace be upon him.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

summary.en: Saved from Pharaoh as a baby, called by Allah at the fire, he led his people out of Egypt through the sea.
summary.ur: بچپن میں فرعون سے بچائے گئے، آگ کے پاس اللہ نے پکارا، اور وہ اپنی قوم کو سمندر کے راستے مصر سے نکال لائے۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
No prophet is named in the Quran more often than Musa, peace be upon him.
His is a story of a baby on a river, a voice from a fire, a tyrant king, and a sea that opened in two.
It begins in Egypt, under Firawn, the Pharaoh.
He ruled the land with cruelty.
He divided its people, and oppressed the Children of Israel, killing their baby boys and sparing their girls.
Into that fear, Musa was born.
And Allah inspired his mother:
Nurse him.
And when you fear for him, put him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve.
We will return him to you, and make him one of the messengers.
So she placed her baby in a box and set it on the river.
And the river carried him, of all places, to the palace of Firawn.
Firawn's wife saw the child and loved him.
She said: a comfort for my eyes and yours.
Do not kill him.
Perhaps he will be of benefit to us, or we will adopt him as a son.
But the baby would not feed from any nurse.
Musa's sister, who had followed the box along the river, said: shall I show you a family who will look after him?
And so Musa was returned to his own mother, just as Allah had promised.
Musa grew up strong in Firawn's palace.
One day he saw two men fighting, one from his own people and one from Firawn's.
He struck the man from Firawn's side, and the man died.
Musa had not meant to kill him, and he turned straight to Allah: my Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.
And Allah forgave him.
When he heard that Firawn's chiefs were planning to kill him, he fled Egypt, alone, to the land of Madyan.
There, at a well, he helped two young women water their flock.
Their father gave Musa work and a home, and one of his daughters in marriage.
Musa stayed in Madyan for years.
Then Musa set out with his family, back towards Egypt.
On a cold, dark night in the desert, he saw a fire on the side of Mount Tur.
He told his family: wait here.
Perhaps I can bring you some news, or a burning stick to warm you.
When he reached the fire, a voice called to him, in the blessed valley:
Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
Indeed, I am Allah.
There is no god except Me, so worship Me, and establish prayer to remember Me.
Allah told Musa to throw down his staff, and it became a moving snake.
Then He told him to take hold of it, and it was a staff again.
And when he drew out his hand, it shone white, without any harm.
These were signs to show Firawn.
Then Allah sent him: go to Firawn, for he has transgressed.
Musa knew how hard this would be, and he prayed:
My Lord, expand for me my chest, and make my task easy for me,
and untie the knot from my tongue, so they may understand my speech.
Allah answered his prayer, and made his brother Harun a prophet to help him.
Together they went to Firawn and spoke to him gently, as Allah had commanded.
But Firawn mocked them, and called Musa a magician.
He gathered the best magicians of Egypt for a contest on a festival day, in front of all the people.
The magicians threw down their ropes and staffs, and by their magic they seemed to move like snakes.
Then Musa threw down his staff, and it swallowed everything they had made.
The magicians knew this was no magic.
They fell down in prostration and said: we believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa.
Firawn threatened them with the cruellest punishment, but they would not turn back.
For years, Firawn and his people were shown sign after sign, and still they refused.
Then Allah commanded Musa to leave Egypt by night with the Children of Israel.
Firawn chased them with his army.
At sunrise, Musa's people found themselves trapped, with the sea in front of them and Firawn's army behind.
They cried out: we are going to be caught!
And Musa answered with complete certainty:
No!
My Lord is with me.
He will guide me.
Then Allah inspired Musa: strike the sea with your staff.
And it split apart, and each side stood like a great mountain.
Musa and his people walked through on a dry path.
Firawn and his army followed them in.
And when the last of Musa's people were safely across, the sea closed over Firawn and his army.
As the water overwhelmed him, Firawn finally said:
I believe.
But it was too late.
Allah said to him: now you believe, when before you disobeyed?
Today We will preserve your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you.
When the Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, came to Madinah,
he found the Jews fasting on the day of Ashura, the tenth of Muharram.
They told him it was the day Allah saved Musa and drowned Firawn.
He said:
I have more right to Musa than you.
So he fasted that day, and told the Muslims to fast it too.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
So what can we take from the story of Musa, peace be upon him?
First: when Allah wants to protect someone, even a river and a tyrant's palace become a shelter.
Second: no tyrant lasts.
Firawn called himself a lord, and the sea swallowed him.
Third: when you are trapped, with the sea in front and the enemy behind, remember the words of Musa: my Lord is with me.
He will guide me.
And fourth: before any hard task, ask Allah as Musa did: my Lord, expand for me my chest, and make my task easy for me.
May Allah make us among those who trust Him completely, in every trial.
This was the story of Prophet Musa, peace be upon him.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

summary.en: He broke his people's idols and was thrown into a fire that Allah made cool, then built the Kaaba with his son.
summary.ur: انہوں نے بت توڑے، آگ میں ڈالے گئے جسے اللہ نے ٹھنڈا کر دیا، پھر بیٹے کے ساتھ کعبہ تعمیر کیا۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
Allah calls him Khalil, His close friend.
He is the father of prophets, and in every prayer, we send blessings upon him and his family.
This is the story of Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him.
Ibrahim grew up among people who worshipped idols of stone and wood, and the stars in the sky.
His own father, Azar, made idols.
But Ibrahim knew these things could never be gods.
The Quran tells how he showed his people the truth.
When night came, he saw a star and said: is this my Lord?
But when it set, he said:
I do not love things that set.
Then the moon rose, and then the sun, and each of them set too.
And Ibrahim said:
I have turned my face to the One who created the heavens and the earth,
sincerely, and I am not one of those who set up partners with Allah.
Ibrahim spoke to his father with love:
O my father, why do you worship what cannot hear, and cannot see, and cannot help you at all?
But his father threatened him, and told him to go away.
Then one day, when his people had gone out of the city for a festival,
Ibrahim went into the temple and broke their idols into pieces, all except the biggest one.
When the people came back and saw their gods broken, they were furious.
They brought Ibrahim before everyone and asked: did you do this to our gods, O Ibrahim?
He said: rather, this biggest one did it.
Ask them, if they can speak.
For a moment, they knew the truth in their hearts.
Then they said: you know these cannot speak.
And Ibrahim said: then do you worship, instead of Allah, things that cannot benefit you or harm you at all?
Unable to answer him, they decided to burn him.
They built a huge fire, and threw Ibrahim into it.
And Allah said:
O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.
And the fire did not harm him.
Abdullah ibn Abbas said that the words Ibrahim said as he was thrown into the fire were:
Allah is enough for us, and He is the best to rely on.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
Years later, Allah commanded Ibrahim to take his wife Hajar and their baby son Ismaeel to a dry,
empty valley, with no water and no people: the valley of Makkah.
When he turned to leave, Hajar asked him: did Allah command you to do this?
He said: yes.
And she said: then He will not abandon us.
When Ibrahim had gone far enough that they could no longer see him, he turned towards the valley, raised his hands, and prayed:
Our Lord, I have settled some of my family in a valley without crops,
near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer.
So make the hearts of people turn towards them, and provide for them from the fruits, so that they may be grateful.
When the water ran out, and her baby cried with thirst,
Hajar ran between two small hills, Safa and Marwah, looking for help, seven times.
Then an angel struck the ground, and water gushed out.
It was the well of Zamzam.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said that this is why people walk between Safa and Marwah.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari.
People came and settled around the water, and the empty valley came to life, just as Ibrahim had prayed.
When Ismaeel was old enough to walk and work beside his father, Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son.
And the dreams of prophets are revelation.
So Ibrahim told his son:
O my son, I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so tell me what you think.
And Ismaeel said:
O my father, do as you are commanded.
You will find me, if Allah wills, one of the patient.
When they had both submitted to Allah, and Ibrahim laid his son down on his forehead, Allah called to him:
O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision.
And Allah ransomed Ismaeel with a great sacrifice, a ram.
Every Eid al-Adha, Muslims around the world remember this moment.
Later still, Ibrahim and Ismaeel built the Kaaba together, the House of Allah in Makkah.
Ismaeel brought the stones, and Ibrahim laid them.
As the walls rose, they prayed:
Our Lord, accept this from us.
Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
So what can we take from the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him?
First: the truth is worth standing for, even alone.
One young man stood against a whole nation, and Allah made the fire cool for him.
Second: trust in Allah is never wasted.
Hajar trusted Him in an empty valley, and today millions drink from Zamzam.
Third: what we love most, we offer for Allah.
Ibrahim was ready to give his son, and Allah gave him far more.
And fourth: after every good deed, ask Allah to accept it, just as Ibrahim and Ismaeel did while building His House.
May Allah make us among those who trust Him like Ibrahim, and submit to Him like Ismaeel.
This was the story of Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

tagline.en: Read, in the name of your Lord
tagline.ur: پڑھو، اپنے رب کے نام سے

summary.en: Alone in the cave of Hira, the Prophet, peace be upon him, heard the first words of the Quran, and Khadijah was the first to believe.
summary.ur: غارِ حرا میں نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم پر قرآن کے پہلے الفاظ نازل ہوئے، اور حضرت خدیجہ سب سے پہلے ایمان لائیں۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
In this episode, the night it all began: the first revelation of the Quran.
Long before he became a prophet, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was known in Makkah as al-Amin, the trustworthy.
Even people who did not share his beliefs left their valuables in his care.
As he came close to the age of forty, his dreams began to come true, as clearly as the light of dawn.
And he came to love being alone.
He would take food and water to a cave called Hiraa, on a mountain outside Makkah,
and spend many nights there in worship, before going home to his wife Khadijah for more provisions.
Then one night, in the month of Ramadan, while he was in the cave, the angel Jibreel came to him and said:
Read!
He said:
I am not one who reads.
The Prophet later described what happened.
The angel took hold of him and pressed him until he could bear no more, then let him go and said again:
Read!
And again he said:
I am not one who reads.
A second time, and then a third, the angel pressed him.
Then the angel said:
Read, in the name of your Lord who created.
Created man from a clinging clot.
Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.
These were the very first words of the Quran ever revealed.
The Prophet went home with his heart trembling.
He came to Khadijah and said: cover me, cover me.
They covered him until his fear had gone.
Then he told her everything, and said:
I fear for myself.
And Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, said:
Never!
By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you.
You keep the ties of family, you carry the burdens of the weak, you give to those who have nothing,
you honour your guests, and you stand by people in times of hardship.
Then Khadijah took him to her cousin, Waraqah ibn Nawfal.
He was an old man who had become a Christian before Islam, who used to write from the earlier scriptures, and who had gone blind.
The Prophet told him what he had seen.
Waraqah said: this is the same angel that Allah sent to Musa.
I wish I were young.
I wish I could be alive when your people drive you out.
The Prophet asked: will they drive me out?
Waraqah said: yes.
No man has ever come with what you have brought without being treated with hostility.
If I live to see that day, I will support you with all my strength.
But Waraqah died soon after.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
For a while, the revelation stopped.
Then one day, as the Prophet was walking, he heard a voice from the sky.
He looked up, and saw the same angel who had come to him in Hiraa, sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth.
He was afraid, and hurried home, saying: cover me.
And Allah revealed:
O you who are wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn.
And your Lord, glorify.
And your clothing, purify.
And all uncleanness, keep away from.
After this, the revelation came often, one after another.
The Prophet began to call people to Allah, at first quietly, beginning with those closest to him.
Khadijah was the first to believe in him.
Then his young cousin Ali, his freed servant Zayd ibn Harithah, and his close friend Abu Bakr, who brought many others to Islam.
For the next twenty-three years, the Quran kept coming down, a little at a time, until it was complete.
So what can we take from the beginning of the revelation?
First: the very first word of the Quran was:
Read.
Seeking knowledge, in the name of Allah, is at the heart of our religion.
Second: look at Khadijah.
When the Prophet was afraid, she did not doubt him for a moment.
She reminded him of his good character, and believed in him before anyone else.
The Prophet said that the best of the women of her time was Maryam, and the best of the women of her time was Khadijah.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Third: good character is never wasted.
Khadijah knew that Allah would not disgrace a man who kept family ties, helped the weak and honoured his guests.
The good we do stays with us.
May Allah make us people of the Quran, who read it, understand it, and live by it.
This was the story of the first revelation.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

tagline.en: A small band, and the help of Allah
tagline.ur: چھوٹا سا لشکر، اور اللہ کی مدد

tagline.en: A night journey to the heavens
tagline.ur: ایک رات، آسمانوں تک کا سفر

summary.en: In one night, Allah took His Messenger, peace be upon him, from Makkah to Jerusalem and up through the seven heavens, and gave his nation the five daily prayers.
summary.ur: ایک ہی رات میں اللہ نے اپنے رسول صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کو مکہ سے بیت المقدس اور پھر ساتوں آسمانوں تک سیر کرائی، اور امت کو پانچ نمازوں کا تحفہ عطا فرمایا۔

cues.text: Assalamu alaikum, and welcome to Stories of the Prophets.
In this episode, a night unlike any other in the life of our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
They were hard years in Makkah.
The Prophet had lost his beloved wife Khadijah, and his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him.
The people of Quraysh had grown harsher, and the people of Taif had driven him away with stones.
Then, in one night, Allah took His Messenger from Makkah to Jerusalem, and from Jerusalem up through the seven heavens.
The scholars differ about the exact date, but they agree that it happened in Makkah, before the Hijrah.
Allah opens a whole surah of the Quran with this night:
Exalted is He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa,
whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs.
Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
The journey from Makkah to Jerusalem is called al-Isra, the Night Journey.
And the ascent from there to the heavens is called al-Miraj.
The Prophet described that night himself.
He said: the roof of my house was opened while I was in Makkah, and Jibreel came down.
He opened my chest, and washed it with the water of Zamzam.
Then he brought a vessel of gold, full of wisdom and faith, poured it into my chest, and closed it.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Then he was brought an animal called al-Buraq.
It was white, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, and each of its steps reached as far as its eye could see.
The Prophet said:
I rode it until I came to Bayt al-Maqdis, in Jerusalem.
I tied it to the ring where the prophets used to tie their animals.
Then I entered the mosque, and prayed two rakahs there.
And there, the prophets of Allah were gathered.
When the time for prayer came, the Prophet led them all in prayer.
Musa, Ibrahim, Isa, and the prophets before them, praying behind the last of the messengers.
This was reported by Imam Muslim.
Then Jibreel brought him two vessels, one of wine and one of milk.
The Prophet chose the milk.
And Jibreel said: you have chosen the fitrah, the natural way that Allah created people upon.
In the narration of Imam al-Bukhari, Jibreel said: had you taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray.
Then Jibreel took him up to the nearest heaven, and asked for it to be opened.
It was said: who is it?
He said:
Jibreel.
It was said: and who is with you?
He said:
Muhammad.
It was said: has he been sent for?
He said: yes.
And it was said: welcome to him.
What an excellent visit this is.
In the first heaven, he met Adam, the father of mankind,
who greeted him and said: welcome to the righteous son, and the righteous prophet.
In the second heaven, he met two cousins:
Yahya, and Isa son of Maryam.
In the third, he met Yusuf, who had been given half of all beauty.
In the fourth, he met Idris, of whom Allah says: and We raised him to a high station.
In the fifth, he met Harun.
And each one of them welcomed him, saying: welcome to the righteous brother, and the righteous prophet.
In the sixth heaven, he met Musa.
And when the Prophet passed on, Musa wept.
He was asked: why do you weep?
He said: because a young man has been sent after me, and more of his nation will enter Paradise than of mine.
The scholars explain that this was not envy.
Musa wept out of sorrow for his own people, and the good they had missed.
Then, in the seventh heaven, he met Ibrahim, the friend of Allah,
sitting with his back against al-Bayt al-Mamur, the Frequented House.
Every day, seventy thousand angels enter it to worship, and they never come back to it again.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Seventy thousand every day, never returning.
Think how many angels Allah has created, all of them worshipping Him, and never disobeying.
Then the Prophet was taken up to Sidrat al-Muntaha, the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.
Its fruits were like great clay jars, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants.
And when the command of Allah covered it, it changed, until no one among the creation of Allah could describe its beauty.
There, the Prophet saw Jibreel in his true form, the form in which Allah created him.
Allah says:
And he certainly saw him in another descent, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary,
near which is the Garden of Refuge, when the Lote Tree was covered by what covered it.
His sight did not swerve, nor did it go beyond.
He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.
Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, asked the Prophet about these verses.
He said: that was Jibreel.
I never saw him in the form in which he was created, except these two times.
This was reported by Imam Muslim.
The Prophet was also shown things of the unseen.
He said: when I was taken up, I passed by people with nails of copper, scratching their own faces and chests.
I said: who are these, O Jibreel?
He said: these are the ones who ate the flesh of people, and attacked their honour.
This was reported by Abu Dawud.
It is a warning for every one of us about backbiting.
And he was shown Paradise.
He said: in it were domes of pearl, and its soil was musk.
Then Allah gave His Messenger a gift for his nation.
He made fifty prayers a day obligatory upon them.
On his way down, the Prophet passed by Musa, who asked: what has your Lord made obligatory on your nation?
He said: fifty prayers.
Musa said: go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it lighter, for your nation will not be able to bear it.
I have tested people before you, and I struggled hard with the Children of Israel.
So the Prophet went back, again and again, and each time Allah made it lighter, until it was five prayers.
Musa told him to go back once more.
But the Prophet said:
I have asked my Lord until I feel shy.
I am content, and I submit.
Then a caller called out:
I have made My obligation firm, and I have made it light for My servants.
And in another narration, Allah said: they are five, and they are fifty.
My word does not change.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Five prayers in our day, with the reward of fifty.
Abdullah ibn Masud said that on that night, the Prophet was given three things: the five prayers, the closing verses of Surah al-Baqarah,
and the promise that whoever of his nation dies without worshipping anything besides Allah, his major sins may be forgiven.
This was reported by Imam Muslim.
In the morning, the Prophet told the people of Makkah what had happened.
Quraysh laughed and mocked.
A journey to Jerusalem took them a month by camel, and a month to return.
How could anyone go there and back in a single night?
They tested him, asking him to describe Bayt al-Maqdis.
The Prophet said:
Allah raised Bayt al-Maqdis up before me, and I described its signs to them, while I was looking at it.
This was reported by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim.
Some people ran to Abu Bakr, sure that this would turn him away.
And Abu Bakr said: if he said it, then he has spoken the truth.
I believe him about something even greater than that: news from the heavens, morning and evening.
This was reported by al-Hakim.
And from that day, he was called as-Siddiq, the one who affirms the truth.
So what can we take from this night?
First: after hardship comes ease.
This journey came after the years of grief and rejection.
When the people of the earth turned the Prophet away, the heavens opened their gates to welcome him.
Second: the prayer.
Most of the commands of Islam came down to the earth with Jibreel.
But the prayer was made obligatory in the heavens, on the night of the Miraj.
Five prayers, with the reward of fifty.
So how can we leave it, or delay it, or pray it with hearts that are somewhere else?
Third: look at the faith of Abu Bakr.
He did not need to see.
It was enough for him that the Messenger of Allah said it.
That is true faith in the unseen.
And fourth: look at the prophets, Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, all welcoming our Prophet as a brother, and praying behind him.
They all brought one message: worship Allah alone.
May Allah make us among those who guard their prayers,
who keep their tongues away from the honour of others, and who believe as Abu Bakr believed.
This was the story of the Night Journey.
In sha Allah, more stories of the prophets, and events from the life of our Prophet Muhammad,
peace and blessings be upon him, are coming soon to Quran To You.
Assalamu alaikum.

tagline.en: The lesson of the archers' hill
tagline.ur: تیر اندازوں کی پہاڑی کا سبق
